**🗄️ Data Integrity & Integration** | **🟠 Major** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Track the last call’s index separately from `next`.**

If a choice emits indexed calls `0` and `1`, then an indexed continuation of call `0`, a subsequent unindexed continuation of call `0` receives index `1` here. `next` still equals `2`, although the last call used index `0`. Aggregation then appends call `0`’s arguments to call `1`. Store the index of the most recently processed call per choice, and use that index for continuations. Add a mixed indexed/unindexed stream test.

✅ Addressed in commit 4801fd1

Good catch, it was real. Fixed in 4801fd1f. With indexed calls 0 and 1, a further fragment of call 0 and then an unindexed fragment, the fragment was appended to call 1 (it continued `next-1`), and a repeated ID of call 0 started a new call because it was compared with the latest ID seen. The indexer now keeps the index of the call the latest delta belonged to, plus the ID of each call, and continues that call. The new test with that sequence fails on the previous commit and passes now.

@pcbeingused333 Thanks for fixing this in `4801fd1f`. Tracking the latest call’s index and each call’s ID addresses both failure cases. The regression test you described covers the mixed indexed/unindexed sequence. ---
